test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: CSIR stands for:

options.text: Council of Space and Invention Research
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
Council of Scientific and Indian Research
Committee of Science and Iron Research

solution:
The correct answer is __**Council of Scientific and Industrial Research**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)**

 
 
• The** Government of India founded the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)**, as an autonomous body in **September 1942**.
 
• It has since grown to become the **largest research and development (R&D) organisation** in India.
 
• As of **2013, it employed about 14,000 people throughout 38 laboratories and institutes, 39 outreach centres, 3 innovation centres, and 5 units** across the country.
 
• This included a total of** 4,600 scientists and 8,000 technical and support professionals**.
 
• Structural engineering, ocean sciences, a**erospace engineering, structural engineering, ocean sciences, life sciences, metallurgy, chemicals, mining, food, petroleum**, and other fields are among the research and development activities of CSIR.
 
• As the nation's top institution, CSIR is ranked **seventh in Asia**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Societies Registration Act, 1860 allows it to function as an independent entity even though the **Ministry of Science and Technology provides the majority of its funding**.
 
• **New Delhi** serves as its corporate headquarters.
 
• Among CSIR's notable accomplishments are the creation of the l**ight combat aircraft (LAC) Tejas and the supercomputer Flysolver**, as well as the **organisation of expeditions and research projects in Antarctica**.
 
• CSIR also developed a relatively affordable** antiretroviral drug for treating HIV infection**, which compelled the manufacturers of well-established medications to lower their prices.
 
• According to the** Scimago Institutions Ranking World Report 2021, CSIR is the only Indian organisation among the top 100 international government institutions**.
 
• It is placed **37th out of 1587 **government institutions worldwide.
